commits.messageHeadline: Update fixture greeting and README for M3 edit check
Add manual m4-check GitHub Actions workflow

pr.state: OPEN when created; closed with its branch deleted afterwards
pr.title: Update fixture greeting and README for M3 edit check

commitPushAndPr.flow: web client, thread 'm3 approve' in /w/t3flare-fixture: branch picker → new ref t3flare/m4-pr-check (git branch/checkout in the Container), then 'Commit, push & PR': the commit message and the PR title/body came from our text generation (pi-ai through the proxy), git push ran in the Container with the Workspace's Container token in T3FLARE_GIT_TOKEN (the clone's credential helper reads it), and t3 created the PR through GitHub's REST API with the Environment token it read from `gh auth token` (the router's answer).

routerActions.argv:
commit -m Update fixture greeting and README for M3 edit check -m - Add two lines to src/greeting.txt from the web client and M3
- Note the M3 edit-only check in README.md

push.detail:
action 1229ms: To https://github.com/ian-pascoe/t3flare-fixture.git
 ! [remote rejected] HEAD -> t3flare/m4-pr-check (refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/m4-check.yml` without `workflows` permission)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/ian-pascoe/t3flare-fixture.git'

workflowsOptIn.after: opt-in turned off again; PR #1 closed, branch deleted; the Workspace switched back to main

ghNeeds.R6: settled: t3 needs no `gh` beyond `gh --version`, `gh auth status --json hosts` and `gh auth token --hostname github.com` (all answered by the router); the PR is made over REST with that token. Environment variable names t3 set on git: GIT_INDEX_FILE (temporary indexes for the commit-message context and review totals), bridged into the Workspace's harness directory by the router.

fixesFoundByTheTrace: `git branch -- <name>` (t3's branch creation) was classified passive and refused with the Container stopped: now an action

t3's temporary indexes (GIT_INDEX_FILE in t3's temp directory, on the Environment's side) did not exist in the Container (`add -A` exited 128): the router seeds each into /workspace/.t3flare/tmp/index-<hash>/index on first use
push/fetch/pull/ls-remote had no credentials: the router mints the Workspace's Container token (one repo; workflows only when opted in) into T3FLARE_GIT_TOKEN
